Inclination

/in-kluh-NAY-shuhn/ - the stress falls on NAY · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Inclination means a natural tendency or leaning toward something.

Given any spare hour, Marguerite follows her inclination toward the water, sketchbook tucked under one arm.

Worked Example

The twins split every chore by inclination rather than by rule: Nour, drawn to machines since her first bicycle, keeps the mower and the pump running, while Zaid, happiest among growing things, has quietly doubled the garden.

An inclination is a leaning — the direction a person tilts when nothing pushes back. It is gentler than a drive and quieter than a passion: you can note an inclination, indulge it, or overrule it, and the word keeps the image of a slope you naturally slide along.

How Inclination Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

leaning

leaning: a mild, early-stage preference

bent

bent: a settled natural aptitude or liking

Antonyms

distaste

distaste: an active dislike that pushes you away

reluctance

reluctance: a dragging unwillingness to act

How Strong Is It? — whim → inclination → compulsion

whim vs. inclination

whim vs. inclination: A whim is far weaker than an inclination — it visits for an afternoon, while an inclination is the direction you tilt year after year.

compulsion vs. inclination

compulsion vs. inclination: Compulsion goes far beyond inclination — an inclination invites you gently, while a compulsion drags you whether you consent or not.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — in-

Prefix — in-: toward

Root — clin-

Root — clin-: to lean (Latin clinare)

Suffix — -ation

Suffix — -ation: the state or act of

Put it together

Put it together: In- ('toward') + clin- (Latin clinare, 'to lean') + -ation = the state of leaning toward. The picture inside the word is a slope: whatever you incline toward, you slide toward whenever nothing interferes. The same lean gives us recline — to lean back.

Use the root in a new word: recline

Use the root in a new word: recline: The dental chair reclines almost flat, which is the only part of the visit anyone actually enjoys.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral

Inclination is the gentle word for a leaning you notice in yourself or others — an inclination to hum, to tinker, to say yes. Propensity (also in this unit) is stronger and more clinical: a built-in behavioral pattern, often one being tracked or managed. You follow an inclination; you monitor a propensity.
